newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain court to rule on Qatari spy case on Dec 18.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain court to rule on Qatari spy case on Dec 18.

text.p: Bahrain's State Security Court will issue its ruling on two Qataris charged with spying on December 18, a government official said on Saturday.
"The court postponed the ruling until December 18," the official told Reuters. The defence had requested more documents, he added.
The trial of Fahad Hamad Abdullah al-Baker and Salwa Jassim Mohammed Fakhri began on December 4 and resumed on Saturday.
They are accused of gathering intelligence for the Qatari government and accepting money from Doha to undermine Bahrain's security. Qatar denies the two were spies.
If convicted, the man and woman face execution or long prison terms. The court's ruling cannot be appealed. It normally holds two or three session before making its judgment.
Last week Qatar accused Bahrain of torturing al-Baker and said the trial "set a dangerous precedent in Gulf ties". Bahrain denied the allegation.
The charges have raised tensions between Bahrain and Qatar, which are locked in a dispute over small islands in the Gulf controlled by Bahrain since the 1930s but also claimed by Qatar.
